title: The list is a conveyor belt
headline: The list is a conveyor belt: half the stays last one morning.
dek: The board's 7-day list holds ten cards. Over 33 mornings it showed 126 different cards, in 159 separate stretches of consecutive mornings. The median stretch is one morning: 85 of the 159 lasted a single morning, and 135 lasted three or fewer. On average 5.3 of the ten cards were there the morning before and 4.7 were new. Long stays are rare and almost all one family: 11 stretches lasted five mornings or more, and 10 of the 11 were Mega Evolution cards. Every one is unconfirmed.
why_now: A slot on the list reads like a verdict, and it isn't one: about half the cards on it this morning weren't there yesterday. The list is slow to turn a move into a ranking, by design, and quick to turn its members over. This is the week to say both.
risk: Staying on the list is not the same as mattering. A card stays while its week-over-week move stays above 5% and its price keeps changing, so a card that fell by half in one reading stays for as long as the week it is compared with includes the drop: the long stays here are partly the rule's doing. Thirty-three mornings is a short window, and a stretch counts only consecutive mornings, so a card that leaves and returns counts twice (25 of 126 did). No sale was checked behind any of it. This is not a read on whether these prices are high or low.
what_to_watch: Whether the long stays end as the Nov 6 readings roll out of the week the list compares against, and whether the median stay stays at one morning once they do, which would make the turnover the list's normal state. Whether a card outside the Mega Evolution sets makes a stretch of five mornings again (Latios Prism Star's was the only one so far). And the label: the morning one of these cards has a checked sale, its row stops reading Unconfirmed.
source: TCGplayer market prices via tcgcsv.com, from the board's published 7-day lists, Oct 13 to Nov 14, 2026 (33 mornings, 330 slots)

foot: Market price: TCGplayer's average of recent completed sales of the same card, condition and printing (help.tcgplayer.com). The counts: the board's own published 7-day lists, Oct 13 to Nov 14, 2026, 33 mornings of 10 slots (git history of data/movers.json; Oct 13 is when the 3-day-median rule began). A stretch is a run of consecutive mornings on which a card was on the list; a card that leaves and returns starts a new one. 330 slots, 126 distinct cards, 159 stretches (mean 2.1 mornings, median 1): lengths 1 (85), 2 (29), 3 (21), 4 (13), 5 (4), 6 (2), 7 (2), 8 (1), 9 (2). 11 stretches lasted five or more mornings, covering 72 of the 330 slots (22%); 10 were cards from sets whose name begins ME (the 11th is Latios Prism Star), and three of the 11 are Pikachu ex 107's (9, 7 and 5 mornings). New cards per morning: mean 4.7 (range 1 to 8); carried over from the morning before: mean 5.3 (range 2 to 9). The table: the four cards with the longest single stretches, each at the last morning of that stretch; start-of-week prices are worked back from the listed price and its rounded change, so within a dollar. The list: up to 10 Pokémon cards worth $20 or more that moved 5% or more in a week; with no checked sales, a move shows only if it's 60% or less, the lowest listing moved the same way by at least a quarter as much, the price changed in the last 2 days, and the card trades. Unconfirmed: no sale checked by Mission Control's Sale Integrity Layer in that window. Not advice.
